definitions.explanation: A profound emotional impact left by something admirable or meaningful. Stronger and more formal than simply being impressed.

examples.japanese: {深|ふか}い{感銘|かんめい}を{受|う}けた。
その{演説|えんぜつ}は{聴衆|ちょうしゅう}に{感銘|かんめい}を{与|あた}えた。
examples.english: The speech made a deep impression on the audience.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{生|い}き{方|かた}に{感銘|かんめい}を{受|う}けて、{自分|じぶん}も{同|おな}じ{道|みち}を{歩|あゆ}もうと{決|き}めた。
examples.english: I was so deeply moved by the way he lives that I decided to follow the same path.

notes:
KANJI:
{感|かん} (feeling/emotion) + {銘|めい} (inscription/engraving). The image is of an impression being "engraved" on the heart.

USAGE:
Almost always appears in the set phrases {感銘|かんめい}を{受|う}ける (to be deeply impressed) or {感銘|かんめい}を{与|あた}える (to make a deep impression on someone). A relatively formal word commonly used in speeches, essays, and interviews.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {感銘|かんめい}を{受|う}ける: to be deeply impressed
- {感銘|かんめい}を{与|あた}える: to make a deep impression
- {深|ふか}い{感銘|かんめい}: a deep impression
- {感銘|かんめい}{深|ぶか}い: deeply impressive
